Define:
```js
export function makeNoise2D(seed=1){
  const s = seed*13.37;
  const hash=(x,y)=>{const v=Math.sin(x*127.1+y*311.7+s)*43758.5453123; return v-Math.floor(v);}
  const noise=(x,y)=>{
    const xi=Math.floor(x), yi=Math.floor(y);
    const xf=x-xi, yf=y-yi;
    const u=xf*xf*(3-2*xf), v=yf*yf*(3-2*yf);
    const a=hash(xi,yi), b=hash(xi+1,yi), c=hash(xi,yi+1), d=hash(xi+1,yi+1);
    return (a*(1-u)+b*u)*(1-v)+(c*(1-u)+d*u)*v;
  }
  return (x,y)=>{ let amp=1,freq=1,sum=0,norm=0; for(let i=0;i<4;i++){sum+=amp*noise(x*freq,y*freq); norm+=amp; amp*=0.5; freq*=2.03;} return sum/norm*2-1; } // -1..1
}
```

```
vec3 col = mix(horizonColor, midColor, smoothstep(0.0,0.18,height));
col = mix(col, topColor, smoothstep(0.18,0.42,height));
```
With midColor a deep violet/magenta (#6a2a6e), the upper-mid sky becomes purple, adding depth. At 7° (height .12), mix horizon→mid 0.66; at 15° (.26), mix mid→top 0.25. This gives a pink→violet→indigo gradient. Nice.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build an interactive 3D web experience from the user's one-word request "3D", delivered as a polished Three.js scene in the empty PlayGround repository.

## Requirements
- Only user requirement: "3D" (no further constraints stated).
- Implied environment requirements: responsive desktop/mobile, working static build served from `index.html`, browser-verified.

## Decisions
- Built a stylized floating-island diorama ("Aetheria") rather than a game, since the brief was open-ended.
- Vendored Three.js r0.169.0, OrbitControls, postprocessing addons, and Sora/Inter fonts locally instead of relying on CDNs.
- Used procedural terrain/noise, instanced trees/rocks/grass, shard-collection interaction, four time-of-day themes, bloom + vignette, and a cinematic intro overlay.
- Added an inline Play-button handler so the curtain hides even if the Three.js module has not finished loading.

## Work State
### Completed
- Static app structure: `index.html`, `styles.css`, `src/main.js`, `src/world.js`, `src/noise.js`.
- Procedural floating island with rocky underside, trees, boulders, grass, path, pedestal, central crystal, 5 collectible glowing shards, fireflies, clouds, distant islets, stars/sun.
- Interaction: orbit/zoom, raycast shard activation, counter, completion beam/pulse, reset view, theme switching.
- Themes: dusk (default), dawn, day, night; smooth palette transitions.
- Responsive layouts verified at 1440x900 and 390x844.
- Playwright capture flow verified with `CAPTURE_URL=http://localhost:3002 CAPTURE_DIR=screenshots/capture CAPTURE_STRICT=1 bash capture.sh`; both desktop and mobile screenshots produced with `auto-start clicked`.
- Console shows 0 errors, 0 warnings in tested flows.
- Shard click tested successfully via `playwright-cli mousemove 798 410` + `mousedown`/`mouseup`; `window.__aetheria.collected` became `1`.
- Completion tested via `window.__aetheria.activateAll()`; counter reached 5 and beam/toast rendered.

### Active
- Final visual polish pass on the captured desktop/mobile screenshots.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Optionally improve remaining visual polish: sun/halo still fairly large, day/dawn palettes were adjusted but not re-captured after the last palette change.
2. Re-run `CAPTURE_URL=http://localhost:3002 CAPTURE_DIR=screenshots/capture CAPTURE_STRICT=1 bash capture.sh` after any final CSS/JS edits.
3. Commit the work (currently uncommitted; server runs in tmux session `aetheria` on port 3002).

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: markup, intro overlay, importmap, inline Play fallback.
- `styles.css`: all UI/intro/responsive styling and font faces.
- `src/main.js`: renderer, camera, OrbitControls, composer/bloom/vignette, UI wiring, interaction, debug hook `window.__aetheria`.
- `src/world.js`: procedural island, shards, themes, lighting, animations, completion beam.
- `src/noise.js`: seeded value noise, PRNG, smoothstep helpers.
- `vendor/three/three.module.js`: vendored Three.js core.
- `vendor/three/addons/`: OrbitControls, EffectComposer, RenderPass, UnrealBloomPass, ShaderPass, OutputPass, BufferGeometryUtils, shaders.
- `vendor/fonts/sora-latin.woff2`, `vendor/fonts/inter-latin.woff2`: local display/body fonts.
- `screenshots/capture/final-desktop.png`, `screenshots/capture/final-mobile.png`: latest verified captures.
- `screenshots/`: many intermediate iteration captures (`desktop-*.png`, `theme-*.png`, `mobile-*.png`).

## Important Context
- Dev server: tmux session `aetheria`, `PORT=3002 bash start.sh`, logs at `/tmp/opencode/server.log`; URL `http://localhost:3002`.
- Playwright CLI session: `aetheria`; browser had to be installed with `playwright-cli install-browser chromium` before use.
- `playwright-cli click "Play"` failed to match; use refs or `window.__aetheria.start()` / mouse commands instead.
- `playwright-cli eval` needs a bare expression (no semicolon); `run-code` with multi-statement `page.evaluate` failed.
- Debug hook: `window.__aetheria.shardScreens()` returns projected shard coordinates; `window.__aetheria.activateAll()` completes all shards.
- Default capture auto-clicks a button whose label matches `Play`; only the intro Play button matches.
- `src/world.js` `createWorld` returns `world`; `world.update` is assigned after the update function definition to avoid TDZ.
- Current theme button active state remains DUSK when themes are switched programmatically via `__aetheria.setTheme` (UI-only artifact; real button clicks update it).
- `.woff2` is not in the runtime MIME map but fonts rendered correctly in Chromium.

229:       const b = i * segments + ((j + 1) % segments)
230:       const c = (i + 1) * segments + j
231:       const d = (i + 1) * segments + ((j + 1) % segments)
232:       indices.push(a, b, c, b, d, c)
233:     }
234:   }
235: 
236:   const topGeometry = new THREE.BufferGeometry()
237:   topGeometry.setAttribute('position', new THREE.Float32BufferAttribute(positions, 3))
238:   topGeometry.setAttribute('color', new THREE.Float32BufferAttribute(colors, 3))
239:   topGeometry.setIndex(indices)
240:   topGeometry.computeVertexNormals()
241: 
242:   // ---- rocky underside ----
243:   const rockPositions = []
244:   const rockColors = []
245:   const rockIndices = []
246:   const rockA = new THREE.Color('#6a5342')
247:   const rockB = new THREE.Color('#9a8066')
248:   const rockC = new THREE.Color('#3d2f27')
249:   const moss = new THREE.Color('#4f6b3a')
250:   const rockRings = 16
251: 
252:   for (let k = 0; k <= rockRings; k += 1) {
253:     const tk = k / rockRings
254:     const shrink = 1 - 0.985 * Math.pow(tk, 0.8)
255:     for (let j = 0; j < segments; j += 1) {
256:       const angle = (j / segments) * TAU
257:       const edge = edgeScale(angle)
258:       const radius = R * edge * shrink
259:       const x = Math.cos(angle) * radius
260:       const z = Math.sin(angle) * radius
261:       let y
262:       if (k === 0) {
263:         y = heightAt(1, angle) - 0.02
264:       } else {
265:         const drop = depth * Math.pow((k - 0.55) / (rockRings - 0.55), 1.28)
266:         const jag =
267:           0.74 +
268:           0.46 * noise(Math.cos(angle) * 2.2 + 80, Math.sin(angle) * 2.2 + 40) +
269:           0.2 * noise(Math.cos(angle) * 5.2 + tk * 5, Math.sin(angle) * 5.2 - tk * 3)
270:         y = -0.55 - drop * jag
271:       }
272:       rockPositions.push(x, y, z)
273: 
274:       const shade = 0.5 + 0.5 * noise(x * 0.18 + 7, z * 0.18 + 31)
275:       color.copy(rockA).lerp(rockB, shade)
276:       color.lerp(rockC, smoothstep(0.45, 1, tk) * 0.5)
277:       color.lerp(moss, (1 - smoothstep(0, 0.16, tk)) * 0.42)
278:       rockColors.push(color.r, color.g, color.b)
279:     }
280:   }
281: 
282:   for (let k = 0; k < rockRings; k += 1) {
283:     for (let j = 0; j < segments; j += 1) {
284:       const a = k * segments + j
285:       const b = k * segments + ((j + 1) % segments)
286:       const c = (k + 1) * segments + j
287:       const d = (k + 1) * segments + ((j + 1) % segments)
288:       rockIndices.push(a, b, c, b, d, c)
289:     }
290:   }
291: 
292:   const rockGeometry = new THREE.BufferGeometry()
293:   rockGeometry.setAttribute('position', new THREE.Float32BufferAttribute(rockPositions, 3))
294:   rockGeometry.setAttribute('color', new THREE.Float32BufferAttribute(rockColors, 3))
295:   rockGeometry.setIndex(rockIndices)
296:   rockGeometry.computeVertexNormals()
297: 
298:   return { topGeometry, rockGeometry, heightAt, groundAt, R }
299: }
